data.gender_notes: Genoveffa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Genoveffa is derived from the Latin word 'Genovefa' which means 'God's source of good'. In Christian tradition, Genoveffa is a name of a female saint, venerated as a virgin and martyr. The name Genoveffa carries the meaning “God's source of good” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Genoveffa usually hope their child will grow to embody god's source of good and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes purity, grace, and strength in faith.
data.etymology: Genoveffa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's source of good.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Genoveffa total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: גנובפה
in_hebrew.meaning: גן ופה - הגן של אלוהים, טוב ויפה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם גנובפה הוא שילוב של שני מילים עבריות: 'גן' שפירושו גן או מקדש, ו'פה' שפירושו פה או פנים. השם גנובפה יכול להתפרש כ'הגן של אלוהים' או 'טוב ויפה מול אלוהים'. השם מופיע במסורת הנוצרית והוא קשור לנזירות ולחסידות.

in_greek.name: Γενoveffa
in_greek.meaning: Γένο-Βέφα, η γεννημένη από τον Θεό, ωραία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Γενoveffa προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'γένος' που σημαίνει γένος ή καταγωγή και 'βέφα' που σημαίνει πίστη ή αφοσίωση. Το όνομα μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως 'γεννημένη από τον Θεό' ή 'ωραία ενώπιον του Θεού'. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Γενoveffa συνδέεται με την αγιότητα και την πνευματικότητα.

in_latin.name: Genoveffa
in_latin.meaning: Genoveffa, illa quae a Deo nata est, bona et pulchra
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Genoveffa derivatur ex Latinis vocibus 'genus' quod significat genus vel origo et 'veffa' quod significat fidelis vel devota. Nomen interpretari potest ut 'illa quae a Deo nata est' vel 'bona et pulchra coram Deo'. In traditione Christiana, nomen Genoveffa coniungitur cum sanctitate et spiritualitate.

in_english.name: Genoveffa
in_english.meaning: Born of God, fair and devoted
in_english.long_meaning: The name Genoveffa originates from Hebrew and Greek roots, signifying 'born of God' or 'fair and devoted to God'. It is associated with Christian tradition and saintly veneration. The name embodies spiritual significance, reflecting a life devoted to God and faith. Historically, Genoveffa has been linked to Saint Genevieve, a revered figure in Christian history.

data.cultural_impact: Genoveffa is a powerful and meaningful name in Christian culture, especially in Italy and France. It is associated with the Catholic patron saint of the same name, also known as Saint Genevieve, who is believed to have protected Paris from Attila the Hun in the 5th century. This maiden saint is renowned for her unwavering faith, courage, and steadfastness, making Genoveffa an inspiring and symbolic name rooted in European Christian history.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, the name Genoveffa is deeply significant as it serves as a reminder of the power of God's boundless grace and goodness. The 'source of good' in Genoveffa refers to God being the wellspring of spiritual and material blessings. This is a testament that even when faced with adversity, including persecution and danger, one can call upon God and find the strength to endure and remain faithful. Consequently, the name Genoveffa inspires a strong devotion to God and a commitment to living a virtuous life guided by virtue and faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Genoveffa, meaning 'god's little woman,' embodies the humility and devotion of a servant of God. Her name inspires a sense of faith and dedication to the divine, reminding us of our role as God's children in the world.

historical_references.reference: Genoveffa was a legendary virgin saint of the 5th century, venerated in Italy, France, and Flanders. Her life story is a retelling of the myth of Dionysus and Semele, with Genoveffa taking the place of Semele. She was said to have been martyred during the persecutions of Diocletian, around 304 AD.

Genoveffa was also associated with the miracle-working spring at Künzelsau in Württemberg, Germany, which was believed to have curative properties. Her cult spread during the Middle Ages, around the 11th and 12th centuries, and she became a popular subject for art and literature.

modern_usage.modern_context: Genoveffa, also known as Saint Genevieve or Saint Genevieve of Paris, is a popular figure in Italian folklore, and her feast day is celebrated on January 3. In the realm of social media, her name is frequently searched and featured on Instagram, where users might post images of statues or paintings of the saint, or of the beautiful flowers named after her - Genevieve's Violets. On Pinterest, users can find boards dedicated to Genevieve and her story, filled with images of her iconography, as well as recipes for traditional Italian dishes named after her. On Wikipedia, one can read in depth about her life, miracles, and the various artistic depictions of her throughout history.
